links.outcome: Perceived versus actual documentation time change after AI scribe adoption
links.effect: 86.5% perceived DocTime reductions, but no overall association between perceived and actual change (OR 0.975; P=.144); actual savings uneven, concentrated in physicians with higher baseline DocTime.
links.quote: Although the majority of physicians perceived reductions in DocTime (86.5%) following AI scribe adoption, there was no overall association between perceived reductions and actual changes in DocTime (OR, 0.975; P  = .144).

links.outcome: Whether baseline documentation time modifies DocTime reduction from AI scribe use
links.effect: Each additional 10% of encounters with scribe use cut DocTime by just over 30 seconds per scheduled hour (P<.001); less-efficient physicians with higher baseline DocTime realized most savings.
links.quote: This effect was modified by baseline DocTime, with less-efficient physicians realizing the majority of time savings.

screen.reason: Evaluates the actual and perceived impact on documentation time of deploying an AI scribe in real clinical practice across 310 ambulatory physicians.
